parsed.why: Unenforced sodomy statute, but documented police detention and public humiliation of men dressed as women, no anti-discrimination recourse, and lethal anti-LGBT violence with no hate-crime response. Evidence dated (2004-2014); thin current record extrapolates toward persistent presentation-based police risk.

Active sodomy enforcement, Police Act 35(c) used specifically against trans people, documented stripping, beating, rape, extortion and post-coup torture in detention, killings, banned books; no recourse. State-directed organised targeting of gender-nonconforming people.

Sodomy struck down and courts functioning, but unenforced immigration statute barring homosexual non-citizens, no safe trans prison facilities (judge's recommendation only), no hate-crime law, documented dating-app ambush violence. No legal recognition is a resident gap.

No criminalisation, no border or facility restriction, protective Supreme Court rulings and visible community infrastructure; offset by documented street harassment and discrimination against visibly trans people in provincial cities, rising political hostility, and no trans-specific violence recourse.

Fresh penal code criminalising same-sex conduct and undefined 'promotion', offence fixed by birth sex so gender-nonconforming presentation invites arrest; documented rise in arbitrary arrests and abuse for appearance alone; no recourse, 98% societal non-acceptance.
